Guttman-style scalogram of person x item observed responses

Source: R/api-plotting-screening.R
plot_guttman_scalogram.Rd

Draws a person x item (or person x facet-level) matrix coloured by observed category, with rows ordered by person measure and columns ordered by location measure. Unexpected responses (those that fall far from the expected category at a given theta) are highlighted with a heavy border so the visual reads as a Rasch-convention Guttman scalogram.

Usage

plot_guttman_scalogram(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  column_facet = NULL,
  top_n_persons = 40L,
  highlight_unexpected = TRUE,
  preset = c("standard", "publication", "compact", "monochrome"),
  draw = TRUE
)

Arguments

fit

An mfrm_fit from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional diagnose_mfrm() output; used to pick up unexpected-response flags when available.

column_facet

Facet name used for the columns. Default "Criterion" when the fit contains it, otherwise the last entry of fit$config$facet_names.

top_n_persons

Maximum number of persons shown (default 40). Persons closest to the median measure are retained when the population exceeds this cap.

highlight_unexpected

Logical. When TRUE (default), draw a heavy border around cells flagged as unexpected by unexpected_response_table().

preset

Visual preset.

draw

If TRUE, print the ggplot object.

Value

Invisibly, a ggplot object. plot_data(p) bundles the scalogram matrix and the optional unexpected-response overlay.

Session plot defaults

See mfrmr_visual_diagnostics for options(mfrmr.plot_preset), argument precedence, and appearance when saving or reusing a plot.

Migration in 0.2.4

This renderer is internal. Use the corresponding plot() route in mfrmr_plot_migration; the former exported name is no longer available.

See also

unexpected_response_table() for the case-level review of the cells flagged in the overlay; plot(x, type = "agreement", view = "heatmap") for a complementary rater-pair view of the same residual structure; diagnose_mfrm() for the underlying diagnostics bundle.

Examples

# Supplementary workflow: run explicitly to keep routine checks brief.
# example("plot_guttman_scalogram", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_core.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "core-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
p <- plot(fit, type = "guttman", draw = FALSE)
dim(plot_data(p, "matrix"))
# Look for: a clean monotone "staircase" of higher scores in the
#   upper-right triangle and lower scores in the lower-left, once
#   rows are sorted by person ability. Cells circled by the
#   unexpected-response overlay break the staircase and warrant
#   case-level review with `unexpected_response_table()`.
} # }
